digest.component_or_area: bridge surface expansion across library and MCP
propositions: Bridge surface operations (preview, sync, status, pause, resume, check_access) must be exposed through public library exports and registered as typed MCP tools reusing the shared core reconciler route/disposition seam.

Legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck must remain callable with unchanged signatures, defaults, return types, and exception behavior while internally mapping to the new canonical operations.

New and legacy mutating routes (bridge_sync, bridge_pause, bridge_resume, and reconcile modes that write) must be gated by mcp.allow_jira_sync; read-only routes must not be blocked by authorization beyond existing requirements.

The reconciler helper beneath run_pass() must return typed disposition and pass detail before _finish_disposition() collapses to integer exit code, enabling library and MCP callers to reuse canonical route classification without duplicating or invoking the CLI.
New MCP tools must publish explicit typed inputs and structured output schemas with no mode parameter, while existing reconcile and bridge_fsck tools retain their current schemas and contracts.
